articles.title: Article: Engineering Reliable Telematics from Smartphone Sensors
articles.summary: Smartphones make telematics more accessible by combining location, motion sensors, computing power, and connectivity in a single device. But the convenience comes with a trade-off: device placement va...
articles.description: Smartphones make telematics more accessible by combining location, motion sensors, computing power, and connectivity in a single device. But the convenience comes with a trade-off: device placement varies, sampling behavior is managed by the mobile platform, and measurements have different timing and coordinate semantics. This article explores a six-stage architecture to address these challenges.

articles.description: Mozilla has partnered with Mistral AI to offer Mistral Small 4, an open-weight model, in Firefox's Smart Window AI assistant, now in beta. It is recommended for users in France, the US and Canada. Users can choose among several models, and Mistral agreed to zero data retention. Beta feedback is mixed. By Daniel Curtis

articles.title: QCon San Francisco 2026: How to Kill the Code Review
articles.summary: Ankit Jain of Aviator told QCon San Francisco 2026 that line-by-line code review is already fading, since most review comments concern knowledge sharing rather than defects and over 75% of PRs merge w...
articles.description: Ankit Jain of Aviator told QCon San Francisco 2026 that line-by-line code review is already fading, since most review comments concern knowledge sharing rather than defects and over 75% of PRs merge without human review. He proposed six layers: argue, capture, codify, prove, debate, own. His team merges four times more PRs, with about 40% fewer reverts. By Daniel Curtis
